description: Validated scientific literature relevant to algorithms and scientific data products implemented or maintained in Spyctres. Links are checked before entries are added; affected_code identifies where each reference informs behavior.

references.citation: Cappellari, M. (2017), Improving the full spectrum fitting method: accurate convolution with Gauss-Hermite functions, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 466, 798-811.
references.description: Develops an analytic Fourier-domain treatment of line-of-sight and instrumental broadening that remains accurate near the Nyquist sampling limit. Spyctres uses this rationale for its Gaussian log-wavelength FFT convolution, including an analytic kernel transform rather than a directly sampled narrow kernel.

references.citation: Husser, T.-O. et al. (2013), A new extensive library of PHOENIX stellar atmospheres and synthetic spectra, Astronomy & Astrophysics, 553, A6.
references.description: Describes the PHOENIX synthetic spectral library used by the template backend, including its 2300-12000 K parameter coverage, LTE assumptions, and wavelength conventions. It is the primary scientific reference for the model spectra loaded, interpolated, and fitted by the PHOENIX workflow, and supports the hard guard against using this grid above 12000 K.

references.citation: Ciddor, P. E. (1996), Refractive index of air: new equations for the visible and near infrared, Applied Optics, 35, 1566-1573.
references.validated_via: Optica DOI resolution and Crossref metadata
references.description: Provides the refractive-index relation currently used by Spyctres for explicit air-to-vacuum and vacuum-to-air wavelength conversion. Centralizing this citation makes the adopted wavelength-medium convention auditable and distinguishes it from alternative Edlen or Morton formulations.

references.citation: Carnall, A. C. (2017), SpectRes: A Fast Spectral Resampling Tool in Python, arXiv:1705.05165.
references.description: Presents a flux-conserving method for resampling spectral flux densities and uncertainties on arbitrary wavelength grids. The legacy Spyctres binning routine cites this work; its conservation principle also informs validation of modern resampling paths, although the production LSF implementation uses its own tested log-grid rebinning algorithm.

references.citation: Morton, D. C. (2000), Atomic Data for Resonance Absorption Lines. II. Wavelengths Longward of the Lyman Limit for Heavy Elements, The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series, 130, 403-436.
references.validated_via: IOP DOI resolution and Crossref metadata
references.description: Documents the vacuum-to-air refractive-index convention adopted by VALD3 for wavelengths above 2000 Angstrom. Spyctres exposes this convention as the vacuum-to-air half of the explicitly selected vald3 conversion method rather than silently mixing it with the Ciddor implementation.

references.citation: Birch, K. P. & Downs, M. J. (1994), Correction to the Updated Edlen Equation for the Refractive Index of Air, Metrologia, 31, 315-316.
references.validated_via: IOP DOI resolution and Crossref metadata
references.description: Provides the corrected refractive-index basis cited by Morton and the VALD3 wavelength-conversion documentation. It establishes the physical dry-air conditions underlying the vald3 conversion, which are distinct from the separately available Ciddor method.

references.citation: VALD3 Documentation, Wavelength conversion air <-> vacuum, including the reversible air-to-vacuum inverse derived by N. Piskunov.
references.validated_via: Official VALD documentation page and coefficient comparison
references.description: This is the authoritative technical source for the exact Piskunov inverse coefficients historically embedded in the legacy get_element_lines implementation. The formula is paired with the Morton vacuum-to-air relation, is defined only above 2000 Angstrom, and is retained as an explicitly named compatibility method.

references.citation: NASA Exoplanet Archive, PEPSI Exoplanet Transit Survey (PETS) Data at the Exoplanet Archive.
references.validated_via: Official NASA Exoplanet Archive page; product description and FITS-column documentation inspected
references.description: Documents PETS Arg as air wavelength in microns and states that the wavelength array has already been shifted to the stellar centre-of-mass rest frame using RADVEL and OBSVEL. This is the authority for the opt-in PETS reader profile and its guard against applying an observer correction a second time.

references.citation: Ilyin, I. (2020), PEPSI Spectroscopic Data Systems: Data Reduction User Manual, Version 1.0.
references.validated_via: Official PEPSI PDF; pipeline, wavelength-calibration, slice-merging, and DXT naming sections inspected
references.description: Describes PEPSI SDS reduction stages and identifies DXT as a slicer/side designation. It supports the rule that a .dxt.nor filename is not evidence for a wavelength reference frame, so release-specific semantics must be selected from documentation or headers.

references.citation: CDS ReadMe for A&A 671, A7 (2023), PEPSI spectra data-product description.
references.validated_via: Official CDS ReadMe; Arg column unit and Solar-System-barycentric scale inspected
references.description: Documents a PEPSI release whose Arg column is in Angstrom and on the Solar System barycentric wavelength scale. It demonstrates why PEPSI release profiles must remain explicit and why PETS microns/stellar-rest semantics cannot be inferred for arbitrary .nor files.

references.citation: Verro, K. et al. (2022), The X-shooter Spectral Library (XSL): Data Release 3, Astronomy & Astrophysics, 660, A34.
references.validated_via: Publisher metadata, official XSL DR3 site, and CDS catalogue description
references.description: Defines the XSL DR3 combined-arm, stellar-rest-frame spectral products and their effective arm-dependent velocity resolutions. Spyctres uses these documented semantics to ingest DR3 spectra as separate constant-LSF regions suitable for empirical PHOENIX classification validation.

references.citation: X-shooter Spectral Library, XSL DR3 Data Format documentation.
references.description: Documents the DR3 FITS table columns, wavelength unit in nm, logarithmic sampling, stellar-rest-frame status, corrected-flux variants, and Gaussian velocity sigma for each effective arm/overlap region. The page does not explicitly identify the wavelength medium, so the reader deliberately leaves air/vacuum unknown unless supplied by the caller.
